page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6.3xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance configured with 12 vCPUs and 96.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio (8.0 GB per vCPU). It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The x86_64 CPU architecture comprises 6 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled to provide 12 execution threads. Cache hardware includes 35 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and 32 KB of L1 instruction/data cache. Dedicated CPU resources are assigned via a KVM hypervisor platform. Network infrastructure features a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps. The instance provides no integrated local disk storage or attached discrete GPUs.

Benchmark testing places the ecs.r6.3xlarge within the average performance tier for most multi-threaded and memory-bound metrics. The instance achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 5,949 and a single-core score of 1,169, along with a PassMark CPU score of 11,961.29. In memory-intensive testing, small block cached memory read bandwidth measured 584.87 GB/sec, while large block uncached read and write bandwidths reached 71.39 GB/sec and 43.14 GB/sec, respectively. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng scored 10,482.47, whereas single-core stress-ng performance fell into the bottom 25 percent bracket at 1,310.88. Database throughput testing demonstrated 10.13 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a static web serving throughput of 9.11 GB/sec.

The high RAM-to-vCPU allocation renders this instance cost-efficient for workloads requiring large working memory sets without requiring proportional scaling of processing cores. However, single-core processing throughput and compression tasks are constrained, as indicated by lower gzip compression results. The lack of local NVMe storage necessitates reliance on network-attached storage solutions for persistent data. The ecs.r6.3xlarge is well suited for in-memory caching systems, database operations, software compilation, and enterprise web application backends where large memory footprints outweigh raw single-threaded compute demands.

Built without local disk storage or specialized GPU hardware, the instance relies on network-attached storage and offers a 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations highlight solid multi-threaded performance, including a PassMark CPU score of 11,961.29 and Redis throughput of 10.13 million operations per second, alongside average memory read bandwidths up to 584.87 GB/sec. While single-threaded compute performance is moderate, the high memory density provides resource efficiency for memory-bound applications.
